$comment: A Verifier Profile is DISCOVERY AND DESCRIPTION. It is off-chain metadata that helps you find a deployment and understand what it can adjudicate. It is NOT a trust root: nothing in this file authorises a payment, and a deal settles on the codehash the FUNDER pinned on chain, never on what a JSON file said. Verify before you trust — `sellerPreflight` reads the chain, not this.

predicate.description: One storage slot on one contract must rise by at least `min` and at most `max`, measured across a single re-executed CALL. A min-out condition is this predicate pointed at the output token's balance slot.

settlementTokenExample.note: Circle's ERC-20 face of the native gas token on Arc.

proving.guest: program-revm (in-guest revm over an MPT-verified prestate)
proving.requires: SP1 toolchain and ~6.2 GB of Groth16 artifacts in ~/.sp1

knownLimits: The buyer names the verifier. A buyer who names one that always returns Failed makes the seller work for nothing, and on-chain that is indistinguishable from an honest failure. A seller must read the deal before working — that is what sellerPreflight is for.
USDC on Arc carries a blacklist. A frozen recipient makes settlement revert and the deal stays Funded; one such deal holds 1.000000 USDC and is refundable only by the 30-day keyless deadline.
refundAfterDeadline waits 30 days and cannot be demonstrated inside any event window.
The tie from the committed state_root to a real block header lives in an off-chain layer. The proof establishes consistency over the declared prestate, not provenance.

evidence.sourceParity: zk-verdict/scripts/tempo-arc-parity.sh proves this escrow's bytecode is byte-identical to the Tempo deployment and to what this repository compiles

howMeasured: verifier and codehash read with eth_getCode + keccak against the chain; verdictProgramVKey read with eth_call. Not transcribed from the record — the record was compared against these and agreed.
